meta.title: ML training and serving pipeline
meta.description: How a model moves from raw data to production predictions, and how monitoring feeds retraining. Thresholds and figures are illustrative.

summary.headline: One feature store feeds both training and serving, and a monitoring loop decides when the model must be retrained.
points: Offline: data is ingested, turned into features, trained on and evaluated in batches
Only models that pass evaluation are registered and promoted
Online: the serving API reads the same feature definitions, avoiding training/serving skew
Drift or accuracy drops in monitoring trigger a new training run

facts.Promotion gate: Beats current model on holdout set

data.title: Raw data sources
data.subtitle: Events, databases, labels
data.description: Application events, operational databases and human-labelled outcomes. Data contracts define each source's schema.

data.title: Ingestion and validation
data.subtitle: Batch and streaming loads
data.description: Loads raw data on a schedule, checks schema and null rates, and quarantines bad batches instead of passing them on.

data.title: Feature store
data.subtitle: Shared feature definitions
data.description: Computes each feature once. An offline table serves training; a low-latency online table serves predictions, so both use the same logic.

data.title: Training
data.subtitle: Fit on point-in-time data
data.description: Builds a point-in-time-correct dataset (no future data leaks in), fits candidate models and logs parameters and metrics.

data.title: Evaluation
data.subtitle: Holdout and fairness checks
data.description: Compares the candidate with the current production model on a holdout set and slice-level checks. Failing candidates stop here.

data.title: Model registry
data.subtitle: Versions and approvals
data.description: Stores each approved model with its training data version, metrics and approver, so any prediction can be traced to a model version.

data.title: Prediction API
data.subtitle: Real-time scoring
data.description: Loads the promoted model, fetches online features per request and returns a prediction. Logs inputs and outputs for monitoring.

data.title: Monitoring
data.subtitle: Drift and accuracy
data.description: Compares live feature distributions with training data and, once labels arrive, live accuracy with the evaluation baseline.

groups.title: Offline (batch)
groups.description: Scheduled jobs; minutes to hours per run.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: Batch jobs on the left build and approve a model; online services on the right use it and watch how it performs.

steps.title: Ingest and build features
steps.description: Raw data is validated, then turned into features once and stored for both training and serving.

steps.title: Train and evaluate
steps.description: Training reads a point-in-time snapshot. The candidate must beat the current model on held-out data before it can go further.

steps.title: Register and deploy
steps.description: An approved model is versioned in the registry, then promoted to the prediction API.

steps.title: Serve predictions
steps.description: Each request fetches online features and returns a prediction to the product.

steps.title: Monitor and retrain
steps.description: Prediction logs are checked for drift and accuracy loss. Crossing a threshold triggers a new training run, closing the loop.
